subject: Request: short-lived GPU slice for latency-sensitive model evals
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-lived GPU slice for latency-sensitive model evals

Hi team,

Quick ask from Product/Research: Acme AI (external partner) is running a focused latency-sensitive model sweep next week. They need a small, dedicated transient slice of GPUs (estimated 4 x A100 equivalent vGPUs) for a 36-hour window to run throughput/latency comparisons against our hosting configurations.

Why this matters: these sweeps are sensitive to noisy neighbors and we expect tight 95th percentile latency variation. If we can provide an isolated slice for the evaluation window, we can (a) validate our autoscale/latency SLOs for managed Dedicated customers, and (b) capture per-token cost delta for that workload.

Ask: can we provision a temporary reserved slice (non-persistent, no SLA beyond the window) and exempt it from the normal autoscale preemption policy for the 36-hour window (start: 2026-04-28 14:00 UTC)? If yes, I need a short runbook and a ballpark cost impact by EOD Friday so I can confirm with Acme.

Constraints/preferences:
- Keep the slice small (4x A100 equiv) and isolated to avoid cache warmup interference.
- No long-term reservation; will be torn down after test window.
- If an autoscale exception is needed, prefer a soft-fallback that allows preemption only if global capacity is < 5% free.

CC'ing Marcus and Kim to confirm feasibility and ops implications; Laura, tagging you for product tradeoffs and metrics to capture.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Strategic Capacity Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-lived GPU slice for latency-sensitive model evals

Jonas —

Thanks for the heads-up. A few quick clarifying Qs so we can size the exception correctly:

1) Exact GPU shape/runtime: when you say "4 x A100 equivalent," do you mean 4 full cards or 4 fractional slices (e.g., 4 vGPU slices that sum to 1x full card)?
2) Network/Egress: will Acme need elevated egress bandwidth or large artifact pulls from S3? If so, we should pre-warm artifacts to avoid bursty network noise.
3) Fallback behavior: you mentioned preemption threshold at 5% — confirm whether you'd accept a last-resort fallback to a lower-precision quantized variant (same model family) if capacity drops below 2%. That keeps the test running but changes the latency profile.

I'll run a quick capacity check and cost estimate against Q2 forecasts; Marcus — can you confirm whether we can create a transient reservation that bypasses the standard eviction queue for the 36-hour window and what telemetry hooks we must enable?

If we proceed I'll attach a short runbook and estimated cost.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 07:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-lived GPU slice for latency-sensitive model evals

Kim/Jonas —

We can do this with an "ephemeral carve" flow in the allocator, but there are two operational notes:

- Allocation semantics: we can allocate a 4-slice logical pool (equivalent to 4 full A100s) that is tenant-isolated for the 36-hour window. It will consume capacity from the Dedicated pool, and we will mark it as nondurable so it auto-deletes after teardown.
- Autoscale preemption exception: allocator can mark the slice as soft-protected; it will only preempt if global free capacity < 5% (we can change threshold). We will NOT support >2% fallback to quantized variant automatically — that requires an app-level switch. Ops recommends we coordinate with Product to include a fallback flag in the test harness.
- Telemetry: enable token-level latency sampling + kernel-selection logs for the slice; that will add ~3% observability ingress cost.

I've attached a draft runbook and a short cost estimate (spreadsheet). See attachment list. TL;DR: expected incremental cost for 36 hours is ~USD 1,200 (compute + storage + telemetry), plus a small ops on-call window.

Next steps:
1) Jonas/Product to confirm start/end times and acceptance criteria.
2) We create a short-lived reservation ticket (JIRA INFRA-3421) and schedule the carve.
3) Ops will run pre-warm of model artifacts 1 hour prior to start.

[Attachment: runbook_reserve_transient_slice.pdf (application/pdf)]
[Attachment: capacity_estimate_q2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Inference Allocator
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Sarah Park <sarah@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-lived GPU slice for latency-sensitive model evals

Thanks — this is great and exactly what we need.

Confirming acceptance criteria for Acme: capture 95th/99th token latencies, kernel-selection variance, and per-token cost delta between our default hosted config and the dedicated slice. Start window confirmed: 2026-04-28 14:00 UTC; teardown: 2026-04-30 02:00 UTC (36 hours).

Action items assigned:
- Jonas: create JIRA INFRA-3421 and attach the runbook + spreadsheet; request ops carve.
- Marcus: set up the ephemeral carve with soft-protect threshold at 5% and enable token-level latency sampling. Pre-warm artifacts 1 hour prior.
- Kimberly: approve the temporary budget for the incremental ~USD 1,200 (or flag if this needs leadership sign-off).
- Laura/Product: provide the exact evaluation harness command and fallback flag for quantized variant (if they want auto-fallback during runs).

Sarah (Acme) — welcome. If your team can confirm the model artifact location and whether you need elevated egress, we'll queue the pre-warm.

Jonas
